b1_kendo_study.title: Kendo's Study Session
b1_kendo_study.beats:
Evenings in the week before the final exams, in the Class 1-B Dorm Lounge at U.A. Academy. Itsuka Kendo has pushed the tables together, written a schedule on the whiteboard (hero law, then math, then modern literature, ten-minute breaks strictly enforced) and assigned tutors by subject: Juzo Honenuki on math, Nirengeki Shoda on hero law, and Kojiro Bondo, quietly the best essay writer in the class, on literature. Earlier the same group held a long table in the Library until the librarian's look sent them home.

Default course, as pressure the player can change: Tetsutetsu Tetsutetsu and Togaru Kamakiri need the most help and accept it the least. Tetsutetsu attacks every problem set at full volume and declares victory before checking the answer; Kamakiri glares at a word problem and dares it to make sense. Neito Monoma sits apart with a closed book, insists he does not need a study group, and corrects everyone's answers aloud from across the room. Setsuna Tokage sends a single floating piece to peek at his notes and reports that they are color-coded. Kendo has heard from an upperclassman that the practical will be robots again, the same as the entrance exam, and passes it on with a warning that it is only a rumor; the room relaxes about the practical and dreads the written test. Nobody here knows the real format.

The party can tutor or be tutored, broker a truce between Kamakiri and an equation, or draw Monoma into the group without letting him win the argument. Kendo will take the hardest student herself unless someone offers; noticing that she has not opened her own books all week, and doing something about it, is a quiet win.

The event is complete when the night's practice quiz is graded and Kendo sends everyone to bed, or the party leaves.
